synopsis: NASA JPL contracted Duality for RACER Phase II in September 2024, providing documented government use of the digital-twin simulation platform also used for RACER-Sim [f8422, f15834]. The corpus identifies DARPA RACER-Sim and NASA JPL as independent evidence of Duality AI Falcon's military off-road use, but reports no demonstrated construction or mining use [f8690, f8978, f15889]. Separately, Project Chrono lists JPL alongside US Army ground-vehicle organizations and NREL as users [f8497, f8676]. Chrono's tool-table entry attaches both vendor and independent evidence, while its vendor off-road evidence also mentions deformable terrain; these facts do not specify JPL's particular Chrono application [f8676, f9023].

relations.note: Both report JPL's September 2024 RACER Phase II contract for Duality's platform.
Both list US Army organizations, NREL and JPL as Project Chrono users.
Both identify DARPA RACER-Sim and NASA JPL as independent Falcon use evidence.
Glossary adds the absence of demonstrated construction or mining use.
Glossary characterizes the evidence as military off-road and identifies an application gap.
The documented JPL contract supports the glossary's claim of Falcon military off-road use.
The JPL contract supplies a concrete event behind the independent-use evidence.
Vendor off-road entry repeats the user list and adds deformable terrain.
The off-road entry adds deformable terrain to Chrono's listed-user evidence.
